title: stochastic-throughput-drop-investigation-scratchpad
content:
Context:
This is a scratchpad for the intermittent throughput drops we observed across Dedicated GPU Pool G-Pool-3 during the last two weeks of Nov–Dec deployments. The symptom is stochastic 20–60% drop in token/sec for short (~2–10 minute) windows affecting a subset of hosts in the pool. Noticed by customers running low-latency chat workloads and by internal canaries.

Why this is different from previous noisy-neighbor docs:
- Drops are short-lived and not always correlated with high overall GPU util.
- We see p95/p99 latency regressions for small request sizes despite low queue length.
- Autoscaler oscillations suspected for a subset of incidents (rapid scale up/down every ~5m).

High-level hypothesis list (ordered by confidence):
1) Scheduler preemption/CPU starvation: GPU kernel launches are delayed by host-level CPU contention or bursty system processes (cron, backups).
2) NVLink contention or PCIe renegotiation events causing short stalls for a single GPU within a multi-GPU host.
3) Driver-level kernel bug triggered by certain model/quantized kernel paths (seen after 2025-10-19 runtime bump).
4) Autoscaler cooldown misconfiguration causing rapid worker churn that disrupts steady-state batch formation.
5) Noisy tenant doing high memcopy/large-batch throughput suddenly interfering with small, low-latency requests.

Observed signals (screenshot descriptions converted to text):
- Host gpool-3b-12: 2025-12-02 03:14–03:16 UTC: GPU util avg 42% -> drops to 15% for 3m; NVML reports GPU PCIe read throughput spike, small but bursty.
- Kernel log: repeated 'gpu-reset' not seen, but 'nvidia-mig: parent device busy' (low level).
- Per-request latency: p50 unchanged, p95 jumped x3 for 4 minutes, p99 had a 20s tail on long requests.
- Autoscaler logs: scale-down event at 03:10UTC, scale-up at 03:12UTC onto same nodes; decisions based on 'queue_length' metric with a 2m aggregation window.

Quick triage checklist we used on-call (notes):
- Confirm scope: run `curl` canaries against same route (canary-token) for 15 minutes and check if repros.
- SSH to impacted host, run `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,temperature.gpu --format=csv -l 1` for sampling.
- Check dmesg for PCIe/driver resets: `dmesg | egrep -i "nvrm|nvlink|pci.*error|gpu reset|nvidia"`
- Check CPU steal and load: `sar -u` and `top -H -p <pid>`; look for processes with high syscall rates.
- Look at autoscaler decisions window: `kubectl logs deploy/autoscaler -n infra | grep "decision" | grep <time-window>`

Experiment log (each experiment run with exact steps & result):
1) Worker QoS pinning experiment (2025-12-05) by Jonah:
   - Action: Set systemd slice to reduce host-level user process CPU sloops on suspected nodes (`systemctl set-property --runtime user.slice CPUShares=256`).
   - Observation: During 36h window, 2 transient drops occurred vs baseline 6; p95 dist improved ~12% on average.
   - Conclusion: CPU contention is contributory. Follow-up: add CPU shares enforcement at host bootstrap.

2) NVLink stress reproduction (2025-12-11) by Marta:
   - Action: Run synthetic memcopy-heavy workload between GPUs using micro-benchmarks (nccl tests) for 1h while running small LLM inferences on same host.
   - Observation: Small but reproducible p95 spikes occurred when memcopy bandwidth peaked (>70% of link). No driver resets.
   - Conclusion: NVLink saturation can create short stalls for small batches. Consider scheduling heuristics to avoid heavy inter-GPU memcopy on latency-sensitive hosts.

3) Autoscaler cooldown tuning (2025-12-18) by Ethan:
   - Action: Increased scale-down cooldown from 3m to 10m and scale-up aggregation window from 2m->5m in staging pool.
   - Observation: Oscillation frequency reduced dramatically; incidents that correlated with churn dropped by ~80% on staging.
   - Conclusion: Autoscaler misconfiguration was amplifying short transients. Patch candidate: default cooldowns tuned per workload class.

4) Driver rollback test (2026-01-14) by Priya:
   - Action: Rolled back runtime drivers on three nodes to the previous release (2025-10-02).
   - Observation: No incidents for 4 days but sample size small; other pooled nodes still had occasional drops.
   - Conclusion: Driver bump may increase susceptibility but likely not root cause alone.

Immediate runbook draft (for oncall SRE):
- If throughput drop observed >10% affecting >2 hosts:
  1) Mark incident: SRE-4921 (create if missing) and post to #sre-dedicated with summary and impact.
  2) Check autoscaler events in last 10m. If scale events exist around onset, temporarily set autoscaler to manual (scale to current desired) to stop churn: `kubectl scale --replicas=<current> deployment/g-pool-3-controller -n infra`.
  3) Run host triangulation on Cloud console: pick hosts with CPU steal>10% or dmesg PCIe errors. Isolate host(s) by cordon+drain targeting evictable pods only. Use `kubectl cordon` then `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`.
  4) If isolation removes incidents, collect kernel logs and `nvidia-smi` sample and escalate to infra-kernel team with attached logs.
  5) If isolation doesn't help, check for NVLink memcopy spikes on hosts: run `nvidia-smi dmon -s u` and NCCL monitoring in parallel. Consider moving large-batch tenants off host.
  6) If autoscaler is culprit (rapid up/down within 10m), set cooldowns longer and push hotfix to staging config: increase scale_down_cooldown to 10m and increase aggregation window. Link: github.com/redwood-inference/rebalancer/pull/128

Longer-term mitigations (proposal):
- Enforce host-level CPU QoS: systemd slice changes in node bootstrap to prevent noisy process stealing compute from runtime. (Owner: Jonah, ETA: 2026-03-01).
- Scheduler change: add label for 'latency-critical' tenancy and schedule small-batch low-latency pods onto nodes with NVLink reserved or single-GPU allocation. (Owner: Marta, ETA: 2026-04-15).
- Autoscaler heuristics: maintain a separate fast-path autoscaler for latency-sensitive pools with longer cooldowns and additional signals (p95 latency, not just queue length). (Owner: Ethan, ETA: 2026-03-22).
- Telemetry: Add NVLink/memcopy counters to per-host metrics and create an alert when inter-GPU bandwidth >65% for >1m on latency pools. (Owner: Observability, ETA: 2026-02-28).

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Are there specific models or quantized kernels that trigger the driver sensitivity? (Need model id correlations from model catalog.)
- Could certain user code patterns (large concat ops) cause memcopy bursts? Add tracing or require better batching guidance in docs.
- Is there a better signal than queue_length for autoscaler decisions for low-latency tiers? p95 latency? request rate?

Action item list (short):
- [ ] Attach kernel logs from gpool-3b-12 incident (Aisha) — due 2026-02-25
- [ ] Apply systemd CPU shares on staging fleet and measure (Jonah) — due 2026-02-28
- [ ] Add NVLink metric dashboard panel (Observability) — due 2026-02-20
- [ ] Autoscaler PR for cooldowns (Ethan) — PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rebalancer/pull/128 — merge pending
- [ ] Map affected customer workloads to model ids for correlation (Marta) — due 2026-03-05

Notes to self and future oncall:
- Keep incident scoped to dedicated-latency pools; don't apply the same cooldown heuristics to high-throughput batch pools without testing.
- If you see p99 > 30s for small requests, assume NVLink or memcopy interference until proven otherwise.
- Record exact node kernel versions and driver revisions in ticket; we've seen subtle differences between 525.x and 530.x families in previous trackings.

References and snippets:
- Useful command to sample NVML & dmesg simultaneously:
  for i in {1..180}; do date +"%s"; nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,pci.rx_util,pci.tx_util --format=csv -l 1 & dmesg | tail -n 20; sleep 1; done > /tmp/gpu-sample.log
- Autoscaler debug: `kubectl get events -n infra --field-selector type=Normal"` then filter for rebalancer decisions.
- Quick gist: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infrastructure/tree/main/diagnostics/gpu

End of scratchpad. Keep this doc as ephemeral working notes; when we confirm mitigation merge to the canonical runbook under confluence.redwood.ai/pages/infra-gpu-pools/runbooks and convert the checklist into a formal playbook.
